note: Genus records compiled from general phycological literature with AI assistance. Imported with review_status='draft' until an expert reviews them. Taxonomy and photos are added from GBIF at import time.

genera.description: Filamentous, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium that has spread from tropical waters into temperate lakes and reservoirs. Now often placed in Raphidiopsis. A major concern for drinking-water supplies.
genera.morphology: Straight or coiled trichomes without sheaths; terminal, drop-shaped heterocytes and akinetes set slightly away from the trichome end.

toxin.health_effects: Liver and kidney damage from cylindrospermopsin; neurotoxic effects from saxitoxin-producing strains.

ecology.habitat: Planktonic in lakes, reservoirs and slow rivers
ecology.bloom_conditions: Warm, stable, often turbid water; tolerates low light

genera.description: Large filamentous cyanobacterium forming dense mats in marine and fresh waters. Several former species have been moved to Moorea and Microseira.
genera.morphology: Wide trichomes with short, disc-like cells enclosed in a firm, distinct sheath.

toxin.toxin_type: Lyngbyatoxin, aplysiatoxins; saxitoxins in some freshwater strains
toxin.health_effects: Skin and eye irritation (swimmer's itch) on contact; some strains are neurotoxic.

ecology.habitat: Benthic mats on sediment, rocks and seagrass; floating mats
ecology.indicator_of: Nutrient enrichment, especially iron and phosphorus

genera.description: Bloom-forming filamentous cyanobacterium typical of brackish waters such as the Baltic Sea and coastal lagoons.
genera.morphology: Trichomes of short, disc-shaped cells with gas vesicles; intercalary heterocytes at regular intervals.

toxin.health_effects: Liver damage; animal deaths have followed exposure to scums.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Warm, calm summers with low nitrogen to phosphorus ratios

genera.description: Small planktonic, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium of warm, often alkaline or saline lakes.
genera.morphology: Short, often spirally coiled trichomes with heterocytes at both ends formed in pairs.

toxin.health_effects: Potential liver toxicity where microcystin-producing strains occur.

ecology.habitat: Plankton of shallow lakes and ponds

genera.description: Colonial cyanobacterium forming visible spherical colonies, notable for blooming in clear, low-nutrient lakes by taking up phosphorus from sediments.
genera.morphology: Radiating, tapering trichomes with a basal heterocyte and akinete, forming hairy colonies about 1–2 mm across.

toxin.health_effects: Possible liver toxicity and skin irritation.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Mid to late summer, including oligotrophic lakes

genera.description: Colonial cyanobacterium common in lake plankton; often confused with Microcystis and Coelosphaerium.
genera.morphology: Oval cells arranged radially on branched mucilage stalks around the colony periphery.

toxin.health_effects: No consistent toxicity; treat dense blooms with caution.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Summer in mesotrophic to eutrophic lakes

genera.description: Small colonial cyanobacterium in the plankton of lakes, related to Woronichinia.
genera.morphology: Spherical cells on short, branched mucilage stalks forming loose, roughly spherical colonies.

genera.description: Colonial picocyanobacterium with small cells scattered loosely in shapeless mucilage.
genera.morphology: Very small spherical cells (about 1–3 µm), irregularly spaced in diffuse, colourless mucilage.

toxin.toxin_type: Microcystins reported in a few strains

genera.description: Distinctive cyanobacterium forming flat, rectangular plates of cells.
genera.morphology: Spherical to oval cells arranged in regular rows, forming one-cell-thick tablets that divide in two directions.

ecology.habitat: Plankton and sediment surfaces of ponds and lakes

genera.description: Simple colonial cyanobacterium of small groups of cells in a shared sheath.
genera.morphology: Spherical or hemispherical cells in groups of two, four or eight, each with layered mucilage.

genera.description: Unicellular picocyanobacterium; one of the most abundant photosynthetic organisms in the oceans and common in lakes.
genera.morphology: Tiny rod-shaped to oval cells about 1–2 µm, usually solitary; hard to resolve with light microscopy.

genera.description: Filamentous cyanobacterium with tightly coiled trichomes. The food supplement sold as spirulina is mostly Arthrospira (Limnospira).
genera.morphology: Thin, regularly and tightly coiled trichomes without visible cross walls under low magnification.

ecology.habitat: Benthic and planktonic, often among other algae

genera.description: Helical filamentous cyanobacterium of alkaline soda lakes; cultivated as the food supplement spirulina. Now often placed in Limnospira.
genera.morphology: Wide, loosely helical trichomes with visible cross walls and gas vesicles.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; contamination of cultures by other cyanobacteria is the main risk.

genera.description: Thin filamentous cyanobacterium with clearly constricted cross walls; common in lake plankton.
genera.morphology: Short, thin trichomes of cylindrical cells with deep constrictions; no heterocytes; sometimes gas vesicles at the cell ends.

toxin.toxin_type: Microcystins reported in a few strains

genera.description: Mat-forming filamentous cyanobacterium of rivers and lake shores. Several species have been moved to Microcoleus.
genera.morphology: Straight trichomes, sometimes with hooked tips, in thin sheaths that merge into slimy mats.

toxin.health_effects: Detached mats have caused dog deaths through neurotoxicity.

ecology.habitat: Benthic mats on stones and sediments

genera.description: Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium forming gelatinous colonies on soil and in water; also a symbiont of plants, lichens and fungi.
genera.morphology: Bead-like trichomes with intercalary heterocytes, embedded in firm, often macroscopic jelly colonies.

toxin.toxin_type: Microcystins reported in a few strains

genera.description: Colonial marine cyanobacterium that fixes nitrogen in tropical oceans; its blooms give the Red Sea its name.
genera.morphology: Trichomes with gas vesicles gathered in bundles (tufts) or radial puffs visible to the eye; no heterocytes.

toxin.toxin_type: Some reports of toxins; not well established
toxin.health_effects: Skin and eye irritation reported from dense surface slicks.

genera.description: Colonial cyanobacterium with cells arranged in a single layer at the surface of a hollow mucilage sphere.
genera.morphology: Spherical cells in a peripheral layer of a spherical colony, without the radiating stalks of Woronichinia.

genera.description: Colonial cyanobacterium common on wet rocks and walls, where it forms dark crusts and streaks.
genera.morphology: Spherical cells in nested, layered mucilage envelopes, often pigmented red, blue or brown.

genera.description: Nitrogen-fixing filamentous cyanobacterium. Most planktonic, gas-vesicle species have been moved to Dolichospermum; Anabaena now mainly holds benthic species.
genera.morphology: Bead-like trichomes of round to barrel-shaped cells with intercalary heterocytes and akinetes.

toxin.health_effects: Neurotoxic or liver effects depending on strain.

genera.description: Tapering filamentous cyanobacterium growing on rocks and plants in streams and on shores.
genera.morphology: Trichomes taper from a basal heterocyte to a thin tip, inside a firm sheath.

genera.description: Cyanobacterium forming firm, hemispherical gelatinous colonies on stones and plants.
genera.morphology: Radiating, tapering trichomes with basal heterocytes in firm, often calcified mucilage.

ecology.habitat: Attached in streams and on rocky shores

genera.description: Colonial pennate diatom that forms star-shaped colonies; a classic spring bloom diatom of lakes.
genera.morphology: Long, narrow cells joined at their wider ends into star-shaped or spiral colonies.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; can clog filters and cause taste and odour.

genera.description: Chain-forming centric diatom of lakes and rivers; formerly included in Melosira.
genera.morphology: Cylindrical cells joined face to face by spines into long chains; mantle with rows of pores.

ecology.habitat: Plankton of turbulent lakes and rivers
ecology.bloom_conditions: Well-mixed periods in spring and autumn

genera.description: Pennate diatom forming zig-zag or star-shaped colonies; common in soft, slightly acidic waters.
genera.morphology: Rectangular cells in girdle view with internal septa, joined at corners into zig-zag chains.

genera.description: Long, needle-like pennate diatom; many freshwater species are now placed in Ulnaria or Fragilaria.
genera.morphology: Very long, narrow valves with a central clear area and fine transverse striae; solitary or in fan-shaped groups.

genera.description: Large, elongate pennate diatom split from Synedra; very common in rivers and lakes.
genera.morphology: Long linear valves with capitate ends, rimoportulae at the poles and fine parallel striae.

genera.description: Asymmetric, boat-shaped pennate diatom that often grows on mucilage stalks.
genera.morphology: Valves curved on one side (dorsiventral) with an eccentric raphe and radiate striae.

ecology.indicator_of: Clean to moderately enriched, often alkaline water

genera.description: Wedge-shaped pennate diatom living on mucilage stalks in streams and lakes.
genera.morphology: Valves wider at one end than the other (heteropolar) with a straight raphe; attached by a stalk at the narrow end.

genera.description: Large pennate diatom with conspicuous rib-like striae; common in bogs, soils and soft waters.
genera.morphology: Linear to elliptical valves with broad chambered striae (alveoli) and a complex raphe.

genera.description: Large, robust pennate diatom with a raphe running around the valve margin on keels.
genera.morphology: Oval to heart-shaped valves with marginal keels, wing-like canals and transverse ribs.

genera.description: Disc-shaped centric diatom of nutrient-rich lakes, often dominating early spring plankton.
genera.morphology: Circular valves with fascicles of pores radiating from the centre and a ring of marginal spines.

genera.description: Chain-forming centric diatom producing long, filament-like chains; common in rivers.
genera.morphology: Cylindrical cells joined by their valve faces into long straight chains; weakly ornamented.

genera.description: Pennate diatom forming zig-zag or ribbon colonies in streams and lakes.
genera.morphology: Linear to elliptic valves with strong transverse ribs (costae) and fine striae between them.

genera.description: Very small, abundant pennate diatom that is often the first colonist of clean stream surfaces.
genera.morphology: Small linear-lanceolate valves; one valve with a raphe and one without.

genera.description: Flat, elliptic pennate diatom that grows pressed tightly against plants, algae and stones.
genera.morphology: Elliptic valves; the attached valve has a raphe, the outer one does not.

ecology.habitat: Epiphytic on plants and filamentous algae

genera.description: Asymmetric pennate diatom shaped like a segment of an orange.
genera.morphology: Strongly dorsiventral valves with the raphe close to the ventral margin; girdle view broad and oval.

genera.description: Pennate diatom containing nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterial endosymbionts.
genera.morphology: Curved valves with a V-shaped raphe and strong transverse costae.

genera.description: Pennate diatom typical of acidic, soft waters such as bogs and peaty streams.
genera.morphology: Curved valves with very short raphe branches at the ends only.

genera.description: Chain-forming marine pennate diatom; several species produce domoic acid, the cause of amnesic shellfish poisoning.
genera.morphology: Needle-like cells overlapping at their tips into stepped chains; species need electron microscopy to separate.

toxin.health_effects: Amnesic shellfish poisoning in people; seizures and deaths in sea lions and seabirds.

genera.description: One of the largest marine diatom genera, recognised by long spines (setae) linking cells into chains.
genera.morphology: Rectangular cells in girdle view with long setae from each corner joining neighbouring cells.

toxin.health_effects: No toxin; barbed setae of some species damage fish gills.

genera.description: Small chain-forming centric diatom that often dominates coastal spring blooms.
genera.morphology: Small cylindrical cells linked into chains by rows of tubular processes from the valve margin.

genera.description: Large, disc-shaped centric marine diatom with a characteristic honeycomb-like valve pattern.
genera.morphology: Large circular valves with radial rows of hexagonal chambers (areolae).

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; mucilage from blooms can clog fishing nets.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Late autumn and winter in temperate seas

genera.description: Long, rod-shaped centric marine diatom; some species host nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria.
genera.morphology: Very long cylindrical cells with conical valves ending in a single spine; girdle made of many scale-like bands.

genera.description: Marine diatom forming star-shaped or spiral colonies, common in surf zones.
genera.morphology: Cells with a wide triangular base and a long narrow extension, joined at their bases into stars.

genera.description: Stalked diatom known as didymo or rock snot; forms thick, wool-like mats in clear, low-phosphorus rivers.
genera.morphology: Large, wedge-shaped, heteropolar valves attached by long branching stalks that build the mats.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; a nuisance that smothers stream beds.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Clear, cold, stable flows with very low phosphorus

genera.description: Sigmoid (S-shaped) pennate diatom common on sediments.
genera.morphology: S-shaped valves and raphe with striae crossing at right angles, forming a lattice pattern.

genera.description: Sigmoid pennate diatom, mainly marine; long used to test microscope resolution.
genera.morphology: S-shaped valves with striae crossing at oblique angles, unlike the right-angled pattern of Gyrosigma.

genera.description: Common coenobial green alga of nutrient-rich ponds; spiny species are now mostly in Desmodesmus.
genera.morphology: Flat colonies of 2, 4 or 8 elongated cells side by side; cells without spines.

genera.description: Coenobial green alga split from Scenedesmus; very common in plankton.
genera.morphology: Flat rows of 2–8 cells, the outer cells usually bearing long spines at their ends.

genera.description: Green alga forming flat, star- or plate-shaped colonies; several species are now placed in related genera.
genera.morphology: Flat disc of cells, the marginal cells with one or two horn-like projections.

genera.description: Small, spherical unicellular green alga; widely cultured for research and food supplements.
genera.morphology: Solitary spherical cells, 2–10 µm, with a single cup-shaped chloroplast; no flagella.

ecology.habitat: Plankton, soils, symbiotic in some animals

genera.description: Motile unicellular green alga with two flagella; a key model organism. Some relatives colour snow red.
genera.morphology: Oval cells with two equal flagella, a cup-shaped chloroplast with a pyrenoid and a red eyespot.

genera.description: Spherical colonial green alga of hundreds to thousands of flagellated cells; a model for the evolution of multicellularity.
genera.morphology: Hollow sphere of biflagellate cells, often with daughter colonies inside; visible to the naked eye.

genera.description: Colonial flagellated green alga forming small spherical colonies of 16–64 cells.
genera.morphology: Spherical colony of evenly spaced biflagellate cells near the surface of a mucilage sphere.

genera.description: Unbranched filamentous green alga with spiral chloroplasts; forms slimy, bright green floating mats.
genera.morphology: Cylindrical cells, each with one or more ribbon-shaped chloroplasts coiled in a spiral.

genera.description: Branched filamentous green alga that forms dense growths in nutrient-rich rivers and on lake shores.
genera.morphology: Coarse, branched filaments of large multinucleate cells with net-like chloroplasts.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; decaying mats can harbour bacteria.

genera.description: Crescent-shaped desmid; common in ponds and among aquatic plants.
genera.morphology: Curved, crescent-shaped cell with two chloroplasts and a vacuole with moving crystals at each end.

ecology.indicator_of: Varied; many species in soft waters

genera.description: One of the largest desmid genera; small cells made of two mirror-image halves.
genera.morphology: Cells deeply constricted in the middle (isthmus) into two rounded semicells, often with granulate walls.

genera.description: Desmid with radially symmetrical semicells, often bearing arm-like projections.
genera.morphology: Two semicells, each with three or more arms when seen end-on; common in lake plankton.

genera.description: Needle-shaped green alga, solitary or in loose bundles, common in plankton.
genera.morphology: Very narrow, spindle- to needle-shaped cells, straight or curved, often in twisted bundles.

genera.description: Small, solitary, needle- or sickle-shaped green alga; very common in plankton.
genera.morphology: Narrow, pointed cells, straight, curved or twisted, usually solitary and without mucilage.

genera.description: Green alga with oval cells often held inside the expanded wall of the mother cell.
genera.morphology: Elliptical cells, solitary or in groups of 2–16 inside a swollen, transparent mother-cell wall.

genera.description: Colonial green alga that stores large amounts of hydrocarbons; studied as a source of biofuels and found in oil-shale deposits.
genera.morphology: Pear-shaped cells embedded in a lumpy, orange-brown, oily colony matrix.

genera.description: Unbranched filamentous green alga of cold, clean streams and lake shores.
genera.morphology: Filaments of short cells, each with a band-shaped chloroplast encircling the cell.

genera.description: Unbranched filamentous green alga recognised by ring-like scars at one end of dividing cells.
genera.morphology: Cylindrical cells with net-like chloroplasts; apical cap rings from cell division.

genera.description: Filamentous green alga with two star-shaped chloroplasts in each cell; forms mats in ponds.
genera.morphology: Unbranched filaments; each cell holds two stellate chloroplasts with central pyrenoids.

genera.description: Large, flat desmid with deeply lobed, ornate semicells.
genera.morphology: Flat, disc-like cell divided into two semicells, each cut into many symmetrical lobes.

genera.description: Wall-less flagellated green alga of salt ponds; D. salina accumulates beta-carotene and turns brines red.
genera.morphology: Oval cells without a rigid wall, two equal flagella and a cup-shaped chloroplast.

genera.description: Green alga of rock pools and birdbaths that turns red by producing astaxanthin; cultivated commercially.
genera.morphology: Biflagellate cells with a wide gelatinous envelope; resting cysts become red with astaxanthin.

genera.description: Colonial green alga forming hollow spherical colonies of cells joined by short projections.
genera.morphology: Spherical colony of 8–64 cells connected by short processes, leaving gaps between cells.

genera.description: Green alga known as water net, forming large, net-like colonies that can cover ponds.
genera.morphology: Cylindrical cells joined at their ends into hexagonal meshes, forming a net up to tens of centimetres long.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; nuisance growths in ponds and rice fields.

genera.description: Sea lettuce: a green seaweed that forms green tides on nutrient-rich coasts.
genera.morphology: Thin sheets or tubes two cells (or one cell, in tubular forms) thick, bright green.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; rotting green tides release hydrogen sulphide.

genera.description: Marine dinoflagellate responsible for many paralytic shellfish poisoning events worldwide.
genera.morphology: Round to slightly angular armoured cells with a girdle groove; single or in short chains; plates need staining to see.

toxin.health_effects: Paralytic shellfish poisoning: tingling, paralysis, and potentially fatal respiratory failure.

ecology.habitat: Coastal plankton; resting cysts in sediments
ecology.bloom_conditions: Stratified coastal water in spring and summer

genera.description: Unarmoured marine dinoflagellate behind Florida red tides and other fish-killing blooms.
genera.morphology: Flattened, unarmoured cells with a straight apical groove and a girdle across the middle.

toxin.toxin_type: Brevetoxins; gymnocins and haemolysins in some species
toxin.health_effects: Neurotoxic shellfish poisoning, respiratory irritation from sea spray, fish and marine mammal deaths.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Late summer and autumn offshore blooms carried inshore

genera.description: Marine dinoflagellate causing diarrhetic shellfish poisoning; it steals chloroplasts from the prey it eats.
genera.morphology: Laterally flattened armoured cells with a small head and wing-like sail-shaped lists along the girdle.

toxin.health_effects: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning: nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea.

ecology.indicator_of: Shellfish toxicity risk at low cell densities

genera.description: Unarmoured dinoflagellate; G. catenatum forms chains and produces paralytic shellfish toxins.
genera.morphology: Naked cells with a girdle near the middle and a horseshoe-shaped apical groove; some species in chains.

toxin.health_effects: Paralytic shellfish poisoning where toxic species occur.

genera.description: Large armoured freshwater dinoflagellate with long horns; marine species are now placed in Tripos.
genera.morphology: Cell with one long apical horn and two or three shorter antapical horns, covered in thick plates.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; dense blooms can deplete oxygen and cause odours.

genera.description: Armoured freshwater dinoflagellate, common in lakes and ponds.
genera.morphology: Rounded to slightly flattened cells covered in thick plates, with a girdle groove and a longitudinal furrow.

toxin.health_effects: Not known to be toxic; can cause taste and odour.

genera.description: Dinoflagellate with two large valve-like plates; planktonic and benthic species, some toxic.
genera.morphology: Cells flattened sideways, covered by two large plates, with both flagella at the front; no girdle groove.

toxin.toxin_type: Okadaic acid and dinophysistoxins in benthic species such as P. lima
toxin.health_effects: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning from toxic species.

ecology.habitat: Plankton; benthic on seaweeds and sediments

genera.description: Large, heterotrophic marine dinoflagellate behind bioluminescent seas and pink or green tides.
genera.morphology: Large, balloon-like cell (up to 2 mm) with a single tentacle; green forms hold algal symbionts.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; blooms release ammonia and can deplete oxygen.

genera.description: Benthic tropical dinoflagellate that produces the toxins behind ciguatera fish poisoning.
genera.morphology: Large, strongly flattened, disc-shaped armoured cells living on seaweeds and coral rubble.

toxin.health_effects: Ciguatera poisoning from reef fish: gastrointestinal, neurological and cardiac symptoms.

ecology.habitat: Attached to macroalgae and coral rubble

genera.description: Benthic dinoflagellate of warm coasts producing palytoxin-like compounds.
genera.morphology: Teardrop-shaped, flattened armoured cells forming brown mucilage films on seaweeds and rocks.

toxin.health_effects: Respiratory irritation from marine aerosols, skin irritation; seafood poisoning reported.

genera.description: Tropical armoured dinoflagellate that causes paralytic shellfish poisoning in the Indo-Pacific; also behind bioluminescent bays.
genera.morphology: Rounded armoured cells, often in short chains, with a prominent apical pore and spines.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Warm, wet season with high runoff
ecology.indicator_of: Shellfish toxicity risk in the tropics

genera.description: Armoured marine dinoflagellate known for brilliant bioluminescent red tides.
genera.morphology: Angular, polyhedral armoured cells with thick plates and distinct ridges.

toxin.health_effects: Yessotoxins accumulate in shellfish; human toxicity is uncertain.

genera.description: Large unarmoured dinoflagellate forming red tides worldwide.
genera.morphology: Large, slightly flattened naked cells with a girdle encircling the middle and many chloroplasts.

toxin.health_effects: No toxin; surfactant-like foam from blooms has killed seabirds.

genera.description: Haptophyte known as golden alga; its toxins cause large fish kills in brackish and inland waters.
genera.morphology: Small, oval, golden-brown cells with two flagella and a short coiled haptonema.

toxin.health_effects: Kills fish and gill-breathing animals; not known to harm people.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Elevated salinity, nutrient imbalance, cooler months

genera.description: Haptophyte alternating between single cells and large gelatinous colonies; blooms produce sea foam on beaches.
genera.morphology: Small cells embedded in the surface of spherical gelatinous colonies up to several millimetres.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; foam and mucilage are a nuisance and can clog nets.

genera.description: Coccolithophore that covers itself in calcite plates; its blooms turn oceans milky blue and are visible from space. Now often placed in Gephyrocapsa.
genera.morphology: Tiny cells (about 5 µm) covered with overlapping calcite discs (coccoliths).

genera.description: Flexible, flagellated euglenoid common in organically rich water; some species form green or red surface films.
genera.morphology: Spindle-shaped cells that change shape, with one emergent flagellum, a red eyespot and many chloroplasts.

toxin.health_effects: Euglenophycin has been linked to fish kills in aquaculture.

genera.description: Flat, leaf-shaped euglenoid with a rigid pellicle and a pointed tail.
genera.morphology: Rigid, flattened, often twisted cells with a tail spine, many small chloroplasts and large paramylon bodies.

genera.description: Euglenoid living inside a mineralised shell (lorica), often coloured brown by iron and manganese.
genera.morphology: Round to oval lorica, smooth or spiny, with a pore through which the flagellum emerges.

genera.description: Golden alga forming branched, tree-like colonies of cells in vase-shaped cases.
genera.morphology: Each cell sits in a transparent, vase-shaped lorica; loricae stack into branching colonies.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; can cause fishy taste and odour.

ecology.bloom_conditions: Spring and early summer, low phosphorus

genera.description: Colonial golden alga covered in silica scales; a common cause of cucumber-like odours in drinking water.
genera.morphology: Pear-shaped cells radiating from a common centre in spherical swimming colonies; each cell scaled with two flagella.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; causes taste and odour problems.

genera.description: Unicellular golden alga covered in silica scales and long bristles; scales identify the species.
genera.morphology: Oval cell coated with overlapping silica scales, often with long bristles; one emergent flagellum visible.

genera.description: Large raphidophyte flagellate increasingly common in brown, humic lakes.
genera.morphology: Large, flattened green cells with many chloroplasts and trichocysts that discharge mucilage threads.

toxin.health_effects: Non-toxic; slime threads cause skin itching in swimmers.

genera.description: Marine raphidophyte flagellate that causes fish-killing blooms, particularly at fish farms.
genera.morphology: Small, slightly flattened golden-brown cells with two unequal flagella.

toxin.toxin_type: Ichthyotoxic compounds and reactive oxygen species
toxin.health_effects: Kills farmed fish; no known harm to people.

genera.description: Marine raphidophyte responsible for major fish kills, notably in Japan's Seto Inland Sea.
genera.morphology: Large, golden-brown cells with many disc-shaped chloroplasts and a posterior tail.

toxin.toxin_type: Ichthyotoxic compounds and reactive oxygen species
toxin.health_effects: Kills fish by gill damage; no known harm to people.

genera.description: Flagellated cryptophyte common in lakes year-round; a high-quality food for zooplankton.
genera.morphology: Bean-shaped cells with a gullet at the front, two slightly unequal flagella and two olive-brown chloroplasts.

genera.description: Small cryptophyte flagellate; widely used as live feed in aquaculture.
genera.morphology: Small, teardrop-shaped cells with two flagella and a reddish chloroplast containing phycoerythrin.

genera.description: Yellow-green alga forming felt-like mats on damp soil, stream banks and mudflats.
genera.morphology: Coarse, tubular filaments without cross walls, with many small disc-shaped chloroplasts.

genera.description: Unbranched filamentous yellow-green alga of cold ponds and ditches.
genera.morphology: Filaments of cylindrical cells made of H-shaped wall pieces, with several pale yellow-green chloroplasts.

genera.description: Freshwater red alga forming soft, bead-like gelatinous strands in cool, clean streams.
genera.morphology: Main axis with whorls of short branches giving a beaded appearance, embedded in mucilage; olive to blue-green.

ecology.habitat: Attached to stones in streams and springs

genera.description: Unicellular red alga forming blood-red films on damp soil and walls; cultured for pigments and polysaccharides.
genera.morphology: Spherical cells with a single star-shaped red chloroplast, embedded in mucilage.

ecology.habitat: Damp soils and walls; marine in culture
